item.research_question: How does increasing configuration entropy affect the energy storage performance and domain structure of lead-free relaxor ferroelectrics, and can it enable a breakthrough in energy density and efficiency?
item.processing_route: Conventional solid-state reaction method; raw materials mixed by planetary mill for 24 h; calcined at 750–800 °C for 5 h; ball milled with PVB binder at 600 r min−1 for 15 h; pressed into 10 mm pellets at ~300 MPa; sintered at 1050–1250 °C for 2 h with sacrificial powders; polished to ~50–80 μm thickness; silver electrodes fired at 550 °C for 20 min
item.test_conditions: P-E loops at 10 Hz; frequency-dependent loops from 1 to 200 Hz; cycling up to 10^6 times; charge/discharge tests at 16–24 kV mm−1 and 20–160 °C; Weibull distribution analysis with n=10 samples
key_findings: Ultrahigh recoverable energy density (Wrec) of ~13.8 J cm−3 and efficiency (η) of ~82.4% achieved in BNTFN-1/3 (ΔSconfig ~1.79R).
Wrec of BNTFN-1/3 achieved nearly 10 times growth compared to low-entropy BNTFN-0 (0.39 J cm−3).
Breakdown field (Eb) increased from 24 kV mm−1 in BNTFN-0 to 64 kV mm−1 in BNTFN-1/3.
Theoretical Eb of BNTFN-1/3 calculated via Weibull distribution is 64.3 kV mm−1 with a Weibull modulus (β) of 28.1.
Nanodomain size decreased from 100–200 nm in BNTFN-0 to ultrasmall PNRs (2–4 nm) in BNTFN-1/3, below PFM resolution.
Average grain size (Ga) decreased from 3.0 μm (BNTFN-0) to 2.2 μm (BNTFN-1/3) with increasing entropy.
Discharge energy density (WD) of ~2.35 J cm−3 and ultrafast discharge time (t0.9) of ~30.4 ns achieved at 24 kV mm−1.
Energy storage performance remained stable over 10^6 cycles with Wrec ~5.88 ± 0.14 J cm−3 and η ~85.5 ± 0.5%.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the performance enhancement to the enhanced random field and improved breakdown field caused by increasing configuration entropy, which breaks long-range ferroelectric order and decreases nanodomain sizes to ultrasmall polar nanoregions (PNRs). Additionally, the coexistence of in-phase and anti-phase oxygen octahedron tilts creates strong multiple local distortions that delay polarization saturation and increase energy absorption.
item.limitations: The text notes that the resolution of PFM was insufficient to effectively identify domain morphology in high-entropy samples, and TEM also could not clearly reveal small-size PNRs, requiring speculation based on HR-TEM Moiré fringes.
item.future_work: The authors speculate that if the types of elements continue to increase to further improve ΔSconfig, Wrec and η will significantly increase, and they suggest that high-entropy antiferroelectric materials still need to be further designed or attempted.
quotes: Ultrahigh energy storage density of ~ 13.8 J cm−3 and large efficiency of ~ 82.4% are achieved in high-entropy lead-free relaxor ferroelectrics via high-entropy strategy, realizing nearly ten times growth.
The achievement of excellent energy storage properties should be attributed to the enhanced random field, decreased nanodomain size, strong multiple local distortions, and improved breakdown field.
